item.title: Global Investors Turn Cautious on Indian Bonds
item.description: The rupee is also under strain, with slowing debt inflows coinciding with renewed foreign selling in stocks.

item.title: China Broadens Market Rescue With Tech Stocks Drawing Support
item.description: China is stepping up efforts to stabilize its stock market, mobilizing a range of state-linked institutions to stem a tech-driven selloff. The chip-heavy STAR 50 index extended gains.

item.title: China Vows to Achieve Annual Growth Target After Economy Weakens
item.description: China’s cabinet pledged to ensure the country will meet its full-year economic goal and to forge ahead with implementing policies, after growth slipped below the official target range in the second quarter.

item.title: SBI Funds Poised for Strong India Debut After $1 Billion IPO
item.description: SBI Funds Management Ltd. is poised for a strong trading debut Tuesday after investors piled into its $1 billion initial public offering, making it one of India’s most heavily subscribed billion-dollar share sales.

item.title: NEXTDC Shares Jump After Data Center Operator Wins New Contracts
item.description: NEXTDC Ltd. shares advanced after the Brisbane-based data-center operator said it had won new customer contracts, bolstering its contracted utilization by 11% in the three months to June.

item.title: China’s GigaAI Seeks 2026 Hong Kong IPO in First for World Model
item.description: Jijia Vision is in discussions to hold an initial public offering on Hong Kong’s stock exchange as soon as this year, joining a flurry of Chinese AI firms planning public market debuts.

item.title: Moody’s Flags Rising Risks in Indonesia on Policy Uncertainty
item.description: Moody’s Ratings remains concerned about policy uncertainty and fiscal sustainability risks in Indonesia, reinforcing its cautious outlook and warning that downside risks are likely to persist.

item.title: Korean Stock Traders Slash Margin Loans to Lowest Since April
item.description: South Korean investors slashed their leveraged stock positions to the lowest level in three months, as memory-chip losses halted the market’s rally.

item.title: Global Stocks Lift Australian Pension Funds to 9.5% Annual Gain
item.description: A rally in global equities delivered another strong year for Australia’s A$4.4 trillion ($3.1 trillion) pension fund industry, despite lingering concerns over the Middle East conflict and stubborn inflation.

item.title: South Korea’s Early Exports Jump to July Record on AI-Led Gains
item.description: South Korea’s exports extended robust growth in early July as artificial intelligence-driven demand for semiconductors continued to fuel the economy.

item.title: Australia’s Stock Market Emerges as Haven From Volatile AI Trade
item.description: Australia’s stock market has emerged as an unlikely haven from the artificial intelligence-driven volatility that has roiled Asian equities in recent months.

item.title: Gold Steady as Traders Watch Middle East War for Inflation Clues
item.description: Gold was steady as traders monitored a raft of developments in the Middle East conflict for clues on the energy price impact on inflation.

item.title: Burnham Picks Narayan as First UK AI Minister to Attend Cabinet
item.description: New British premier Andy Burnham has named Kanishka Narayan as minister for artificial intelligence, promoting the role to attend the prime minister’s cabinet for the first time.

item.title: New Zealand’s Faster Inflation Bolsters Case for More Rate Hikes
item.description: New Zealand’s annual inflation accelerated to the fastest pace in more than two years, fanned by soaring fuel prices and bolstering the case for the Reserve Bank to execute back-to-back interest-rate increases.

item.title: Kioxia Bulls Ride Out Volatility With Targets 130% Above Market
item.description: Analysts are maintaining bullish views on Kioxia Holdings Inc. despite a deepening share price correction, saying the stock is likely to resume its upward trajectory once supply-demand conditions improve.

item.title: LA’s $1.2 Billion ‘Graffiti Towers’ Cleared to Exit Bankruptcy
item.description: The bankrupt $1.2 billion Oceanwide Plaza project in Los Angeles, dubbed the Graffiti Towers after taggers spray-painted the abandoned complex, has been cleared for sale and possible completion more than seven years after the original Chinese developer ran out of money.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 20
item.description: Oil held a two-day gain as the US and Iran continued hostilities in the Middle East, while Yemen’s Houthi militants threatened to blockade Saudi Arabia’s maritime traffic in the Red Sea.

item.title: Oil Holds Gains, Bonds Drop on Inflation Concerns: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil held near its highest close since mid-June, weighing on stocks and Treasuries, as an escalation in Middle East hostilities rekindled worries about inflation.

item.title: Oracle Credit Risk Hits Near 18-Year High on AI Debt Load Angst
item.description: The cost of protecting Oracle Corp.’s debt against default reached a fresh multi-year high on Monday while its existing bonds sold off, as doubts grew over whether the company’s massive investments in artificial intelligence will pay off.

item.title: BlackRock’s Meta Deal to Show the Power of $25 Billion M&A Spree
item.description: For Larry Fink, BlackRock Inc.’s more than $12 billion debt sale for a Meta Platforms Inc. data center is the result of years spent transforming a public investments giant into a heavy hitter in private markets too.

item.title: UBS Trading Desk Says Buy Momentum Stocks as Selloff Nears End
item.description: The sharp selloff in momentum stocks may be nearing its end, creating an opportunity for investors to start rebuilding positions in artificial intelligence and semiconductor shares, according to UBS’ trading desk.

item.title: Snap Nears Settlement of Addiction Case Ahead of Jury Trial
item.description: Snap Inc. said it has reached a tentative agreement to settle the second case set for trial over claims that the world’s largest social media platforms are addictive to minors, leaving only Meta Platforms Inc. to face a jury starting next week in Los Angeles.

item.title: DC Readies $1.2 Billion Bond Sale as Credit Stabilizes Post-DOGE
item.description: Washington, DC is stepping up to borrow $1.2 billion this week at its annual municipal debt sale, tapping the market as its credit stabilizes.

item.title: How Trump Plans to Maintain His Tariff Wall
item.description: From the start of his second term, US President Donald Trump made clear he would put tariffs at the center of US economic policy. When the Supreme Court invalidated sweeping import duties he’d imposed citing emergency powers, he used a different provision, Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, to set a flat 10% levy on imports. Such tariffs are time-limited, however, and Trump’s expire on July 24.

item.title: Paytm’s Profit Rises After Turnaround Boosts Bottom Line
item.description: Paytm reported a 79% rise in net profit, reflecting cost cuts as well as growth across its payments and financial services businesses.

item.title: Money Funds Keep Cash Closer as Fed Leaves Markets Guessing
item.description: Money‑market funds are shifting toward ultra short-term holdings and away from assets with even modest interest-rate risk as uncertainty grows over the Federal Reserve’s policy path and the near-term outlook for rates.

item.title: Shipowners Offer Huge Bonuses to Get Crews to Sail Hormuz
item.description: One shipowner is attempting to coax crews to sail through the Strait of Hormuz by offering them an extra six months pay if they’re willing to cross the vital oil channel, offering seafarers a stark choice between large financial rewards and the risk of death.

item.title: The Oil Shock Isn’t Over
item.description: Releasing barrels of crude was the easy part.

item.title: US Immigration Policies Sink Mexican Grocery Chain Chedraui
item.description: President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown is causing the worst rout on the Mexican stock exchange this year.

item.title: National Bank of Canada Weighs SRT Tied to Project Finance Deals
item.description: National Bank of Canada is assessing investors’ appetite for a significant risk transfer deal, adding its name to a growing list of lenders exploring the instruments as a way to create room on their balance sheets.
